#184496. I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1296 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance.
  • According to recent reports, developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal.
  • In a recent development, the first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance. Voyaging uncharted waters may appear foolish to some, yet folly and heroism can often appear the same to the undiscerning eye," so states the voice of Johannes Zuch - creator, writer, director, composer, and 'perceptual architect' behind Leonida's latest favourite indie darling art game, Tenebrae Lux. It's pretentious, it's deeply up its own arse, and it's awkward and off-putting to play. A must-review for Eurogamer.

According to recent reports, developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal. Jason is quick to dismiss Tenebrae Lux in company, but once Cal slinks off home - hungover and dreary - I slide the disc back into my JoyStation console and sink my teeth back into it. Jason loves this stuff, really. He only keeps Time Jackers: Rewind installed so his mates don't judge him.

In a recent development, the first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name. It's Latin for 'darkness and light', or something similar. Is this riffing on Clair Obscur, which is French for 'light dark'? No, it's too cerebral for that - too plodding and navel-gazey. Sandfall Interactive wouldn't be this pretentious. Maybe it's a pastiche of Dear Esther, then, drawing on the tenets and schema of the 'walking simulator' genre and using that washed-out film noir aesthetic. But then, it's too wordy for that, with too many interactive and puzzle-adjacent elements. Ah, it must be mocking The Witness, instead - there's the telltale lighthouse, the 'I'm definitely not telling you where to go and what to do' internal narration, and of course the fingerprints of Johannes Zuch are all over it. Johannes Zuch, Jonathan Blow - see how they braided them together? (Sorry).

Whilst this has been created by Rockstar as a pastiche - as much loving send-up as it is withering take down - and designed to make a quick joke in the early 'Feng Shui' mission, the game is playable from start to finish if you so desire. You boot it up by inserting a physical disc, too, which is funny given the context. And it's good! Well, not good good, but it's a proper brainteaser, and ribs 2016's The Witness with such knowledge and (I think?) respect that it's hard not to be charmed by Rockstar's game-within-a-game. There are collectibles to be found that riff on Mark Z. Danielewski's House of Leaves, too, a knowing nod to the most try-hard of all try-hard literature.

Within seconds of the title screen, too, you're presented with a game-within-a-game-within-a-game. You must clear four boards filled with puzzle pieces as the protagonist mutters something mysterious and weird in his posh voice. Do so, and you unlock the door to the next location. Head up to a bunker, and you'll see a room filled with various clues - maybe it's a flashing lamp flickering in morse code, maybe it's a malfunctioning clock presenting a maths puzzle, maybe it's a pricetag on a record that changes on every visit, maybe it's a photograph with anomalous elements, maybe it's a "Developed Using Zuchworks Engine" easter egg hidden in the environment. You need to keep your wits about you, because one of these clues changes every time you enter - and the clue corresponds to a date that changes on a calendar on the wall.

Sources indicate that you can look up a guide if you need to, or you can spend far too long figuring out how all this relates to the telephone you can find in the room on your own, like muggins here, before opening up the path to the next puzzle. Look at the image below to see the level of record-keeping and brainteasing this bizarre little game prompted from me. I will say, the sense of achievement you get from playing around with this stuff is pretty remarkable, given - let's not forget I'm actually playing Grand Theft Auto 6 whilst I'm wandering around in the black and white murk trying to complete a puzzle game for no actual reward.

It has been revealed that the bunker room is, by far, the hardest part of Tenebrae Lux. From here, things ease up: you need to figure out the right sequence of glyphs on a bridge, and then put some distance between yourself and a curious and rather creepy suited man that's seemingly figuring things out ahead of you in a location inspired by, I think, The Backrooms (or Portal, or Superliminal, or maybe something else entirely. Who knows what Zuch was thinking?).

"With the last enigma finally mastered," the narrator drones in his bumbling monotone, "I step forward into the void, the shadows swallow, consuming all, and then finally the sweet embrace of darkness of which there is no end." 'You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience', Tenebrae Lux tells me, before cutting to the best joke of the whole thing: the credits roll much akin to something Hideo Kojima would produce.

Recent findings suggest that so, what do you get out of all of this? Well - just like real puzzle games in the real world - nothing, really. If you've not completed one of the other three fully playable games in GTA 6, you will get a trophy/achievement. But given the main game is all about Jason and Lucia's desperate scramble to escape the poverty trap, to try and break free of the cycle of debt, violence, and consequence that keeps them clinging to Leonida's seedy underbelly, there's no monetary reward. There's no 'progress' in the sense of the protagonist's shared story.

Even in terms of your own cold, hard, mathematical 'completion' you only need to boot each of the four games up once in order to work towards GTA 6's 100% completion. So what's the point of all this? Why did I spend the better part of 90 minutes trying to figure out how to find a sliver of light in the dark in Tenebrae Lux? The game is a wonderful pastiche in that, essentially, it's not really saying anything. You can probably project some vague meaning onto it if you wish - I'm pretty certain the protagonist literally 'finds himself' at the end - but glib little readings like that are ten-a-penny in this genre.

Sources indicate that I think the most impressive thing about Tenebrae Lux is that it exists. You're teased with it in an early mission - Rockstar may as well say 'look, we put a game in a game, lol' - but it's more than that. This is what happens when Rockstar's 4700-plus developers are given the room to… develop. Tenebrae Lux could very easily have been a non-interactive experience, a quick, cheap joke shown over-the-shoulder taking a drive-by pop shot at Johnathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck, or any and all of the above. Or maybe it could be a 'vertical slice', an incomplete demo, a teaser. But it's not, because nothing about GTA 6 is quick or cheap.

GTA 6, in every single conceivable way, is a premium experience - part-sandbox, part-simulation, part-otherworld. To create not just one, but four fully playable and completable games within that framework is showboating, sure, but to make that game actually good and - perhaps controversially - even better than some of the games it's pastiching… Well, it's just rubbing salt in the wound, really.

A code for the game was provided by Cal Hampton.

Find Orphan Pages and Buried Content: Build an Internal Link Graph for Your Site

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (682 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Recent findings suggest that the pages of a site form a graph.
  • A search crawler usually uses one of these pages as a starting point and crawls through all of the pages (especially when pages are not fully covered in a sitemap).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

It has been revealed that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Recent findings suggest that the pages of a site form a graph. Think of it as many nodes connected to each other via edges. Each of the edges are the links between the pages, and the nodes themselves are the pages. Now if you start to visualize this as a graph, you will rapidly see that there are multiple ways to traverse this graph and reach a particular endpoint.

A search crawler usually uses one of these pages as a starting point and crawls through all of the pages (especially when pages are not fully covered in a sitemap).

If a page lies very deep from the home page, it means that it's not an important page. It's an indication to the search engine that this is not something that you yourself consider important, and the search engine has a lesser incentive to rank this page over pages that are linked better within your site.

In a recent development, the key metric here is link depth. That is the number of clicks it takes to reach a particular page from your home page.

Sources indicate that another key metric is broken links. If you have too many broken links, it indicates to the search engine that your site is outdated and not well maintained, and the search engine will then not want to rank your site.

The way to identify both these problems is the same: to actually walk through your site, do a crawl of your site outside in, and try to figure out what the link depth is and if there are broken links on your website.

Industry observers note that seed the crawl with the home page and all URLs mentioned in the sitemap. Technically, the sitemap is not required if you're doing a crawl, but going from the sitemap will allow us to detect orphaned pages as well.

Sources indicate that fetch the pages and follow redirects as required. Record when you're following a redirect: we do not let fetch follow it silently, we record each hop and add its target to the crawl. Record HTTP errors as they occur.

Drop URL fragments and tracking parameters. Keep trailing slashes because sometimes there can be mismatches around expectation of trailing slashes in different URLs of a site.

#184493. It took me less than an hour to find my first incredibly minor Rockstar easter egg in GTA 6 - but it has some significant implications for Leonida

It took me less than an hour to find my first incredibly minor Rockstar easter egg in GTA 6 - but it has some significant implications for Leonida

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that are you wondering how connected the worlds of GTA 5 and GTA 6 are?
  • According to recent reports, right, if you're reading from this point onwards, you're clearly here for the tea.
  • In a recent development, called 'Body Copy' - a joke I appreciate as a former magazine editor, naturally - this publication features a few different articles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that are you wondering how connected the worlds of GTA 5 and GTA 6 are? Well, I've got some news for you. Keep on reading below if you'd like some very minor spoilers for the early game of GTA 6, spoilers for GTA 5, as well as some information about how the upcoming game links to GTA 5 and other Rockstar games.

According to recent reports, right, if you're reading from this point onwards, you're clearly here for the tea. In the first hour or so of GTA 6, when you finally get control of Jason and head to your first property (the green stilted house) in the Leonida Keys, you will be able to explore a little. On my way to do a workout - you need to keep Jason a peak physical instrument for his work's sake, right? Right? - I happened upon a fitness magazine resting on a table on the decking out front.

In a recent development, called 'Body Copy' - a joke I appreciate as a former magazine editor, naturally - this publication features a few different articles. There's Morning Glory, where Nolan Crockett jacks you with his early workout; Skindecent Exposure, a photo spread about why beaches are 'crazy' places to work out; Shrediquette, a piece dedicated to proper in-gym decorum; and Twilight Tantra, an interview feature and yoga masterclass with 'gerontophile' Fabien LaRouche.

Industry observers note that hang on, Fabien LaRouche… isn't that the French wellness guru and shyster that was a "close friend" to Amanda De Santa in Grand Theft Auto 5? Yes, yes it is. In fact, Fabien played quite a large role in that game, acting as the antagonistic force that eventually fractured Michael and Amanda's relationship. After conducting an affair under the guise of 'yoga lessons', Amanda left our protagonist, and moved in with Fabien, taking Michael's kids - Jimmy and Tracy - with her. In a totally healthy and normal way, you could follow their new life via updates posted to GTA's Facebook surrogate, LifeInvader. It's clear the kids never liked the pretentious, annoying man - but for Amanda, the penny is a little slower to drop. Eventually, Amanda and Michael reconcile their differences - with the latter whalloping Fabien in the process. The married couple pledge to resolve their differences, and Fabien is never seen again.

Until GTA 6, at least. Here, in what we assume is supposed to be 2025 or 2026, it's been about 13 years since we last saw the character (it is widely agreed that GTA 5 is set in 2013 - the game's original launch year). And it seems that the events surrounding Michael and his family really did a number on Fabien. Which - of course - he blamed on the universe, rather than taking any personal responsibility. Naturally.

"Ever since the karmic decay of Los Santos was made perfectly clear to him in the early 2010s, yoga instructor Fabien LaRouche has been on an epic pilgrimage of enlightenment through the remotest ashrams and finest 5-star resorts and plastic surgery retreats of The East," reads the Body Copy article. "Having completed his chakric education and returned to the United States, we meet with him on the final week of his six-month residency at Dwindle Wood Retirement Community.".

Here, the article goes on to explore Fabien's penchant for older women - he seems to like their nature, their desire to learn about self-improvement and wellness, and (perhaps most importantly) their bank accounts. "Being over the hill doesn't necessarily mean you have nothing left to live for," he opines in the article. Thanks for that, Fabien.

It's interesting to see - very early in the game and quite plainly telegraphed - that Rockstar is willing to reintroduce us to people from previous games. This isn't a megaton addition by any means - Fabien was never a 'main character' - but I love that a nod to him, in a feature tucked away at the back of a magazine, sets the scene for more cameos, perhaps, later in the game. It shows us, nice and early, that GTA 5 and GTA 6 are indeed connected. By inference, then, we know that GTA 4 is included in that same picture; there were recurring characters in GTA 5 that appeared in GTA 4, after all - Patrick McReary, Johnny Klebitz, Rocco Pelosi and more come to mind.

Recent findings suggest that it may seem like a small thing, but it's just another example of Rockstar using its expansive toolset, ridiculous budget, and well-established legacy to inject a sense of scale into the world of Grand Theft Auto 6. There are other nods to the universe out there, too. I won't spoil them here, but I've been a little bit dewy-eyed to hear rumours of some of the other nods to Rockstar titles hidden in the world of Leonida: it makes all the experiences I've had in past games, the emotional response I've had to previous Rockstar worlds, feel in some way valid and meaningful here, too. I'm looking forward to seeing what other little secrets await me across the keys and into the glowing neon promise of Vice City proper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that did anything notable happen this week? Not that I can remember. The weather was quite rainy - will that do? I'm just being silly, of course. We've had - and I suppose are still having - an historic week in video games, as Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives. It's dominated everything and I fear it's going to dominate this article too. But a reminder: next week is our "Not-GTA Week", so we'll be making a concerted effort to talk about games, probably smaller games, that aren't Godzilla blockbusters.

As you know, this is our regular feature where we say a bit about the games we've been playing this week. This week, rather a lot of us have been playing GTA 6, as you can imagine, and discovering various things about it. But not all of us. Connor, ever the contrarian, has been continuing his race to level 60 in World of Warcraft: Forever, and he's agonisingly close to getting there.

But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago.

According to recent reports, it probably comes as no surprise that I'm - much like the rest of the world - playing GTA 6 right now. While I found Chapter 1 to be quite a slow start, and where I felt somewhat restricted, I've now started Chapter 2 and found myself enjoying stealing cars, jamming along to the radio, and simply exploring Leonida - and all the strange happenings that come with it. There's so much to see and do!

I'm looking forward to deviating from the main missions for a while to do a spot of bird-watching (I like birds a lot, alright) and seeing what other side activities Leonida has to offer outside of the criminal lifestyle at the core of things. I'm also trying to be the best partner possible to both Jason and Lucia, but I'm itching to cause a bit of trouble soon... Hurting NPCs comes with so much guilt this time around though!

Recent findings suggest that it's slow, it's awkward, it's weird, and it's hard. It's a perfect Eurogamer game, right? Right? GTA 6's in-game lampoon of Jonathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck and - weirdly - Mark Z. Danielewski is a wonderful bit of top-shelf pastiche. It goes to show just how much fun Rockstar had making GTA 6, and the freedom its dev team had to install as much depth and satire in just about every nook and cranny conceivable. Don't sleep on Tenebrae Lux, it's genuinely satisfying to complete.

I'm not, historically, the biggest GTA fan - although I've absolutely got a soft spot for Vice City's sublime mood - so I wasn't quite as excited to play GTA 6 as some. But it took, oh I dunno, about 30 seconds before I was sold. This thing has style. And everything else a billion dollars and some incredible development talent gets you. And it's those because-we-can details that have, in my first few hours, left the biggest impression. I spent a good five minutes just marveling at Jason dance - specifically the way his little stationary wiggle (perfectly timed to the radio beat!) shifts seamlessly into a wiggle-strut when you hit the forward button.

I love the way the setting sun seems to shine just right through the clouds when the moment calls, and those perfect needle drops. And careening through the night - amid the driving rain and smear of taillights, Kylie classic Spinning Around booming on the radio and Jason rocking a recently acquired, slightly improbable hat - this extravagant, ridiculous thing had me completely transfixed. I'm genuinely, unexpectedly excited to see where it takes me next.

In a recent development, assuming there's lots of Grand Theft Auto 6 in this article, I'll save you from my own early impressions of this week's blockbuster release. Instead, you get more tales from an MMO. It is what it is!

In a recent development, I'm level 58 right now, pushing my way into the endgame dungeons. I've almost maxed all my professions, and am gradually getting gear that should serve me well when the raids are added next month.

But forget all that. I got a salt shaker! As a leatherworker, you can buy a salt shaker from engineers for a little bit of gold on the auction house. These are more notable than you'd assume. With them you can make one refined deeprock salt every three days - a high-end crafting material. Rather than hoard these for fancy gear, I just sold 'em back to the auction house. They're current going for 50 gold a pop on my server, which is fantastic passive income.

Sources indicate that this is crucial because I'm currently saving for an epic mount: a process that hit a major roadbump after I unlocked my secondary class specialisation for 50 gold, and then blew way more than that on unlocking all the available skills (that I likely won't use) from my druid trainer (for no good reason). I'm currently sitting on 232 gold as of writing. There's a long way to go to 1000, but hey, that's the game.

Recent findings suggest that I can't imagine anyone changing the radio station when Drive by The Cars begins during that first moment of proper uninterrupted freedom. The buttons to do that might as well not even be there. If you did, we're completely different people.

I'm not very far in but my major impressions of GTA 6 so far are: the performances and their presentation are wonderful, the game controls a bit sludgily and feels like it's not quite in focus on PS5, and I really like DIY.

Recent findings suggest that let's take that middle one, that criticism: I'm sure this will lift as I get used to the game and how it moves, and how the characters work. It's also just a fact of life, so to speak, that it's going to struggle a bit on PS5 rather than PS5 Pro. And I'm nitpicking; on the whole, this thing is staggeringly technically impressive.

The latter point, DIY: it's absurd how much detail Rockstar has put into you doing up your shack. I especially like how it's not boring. A deeper thought related to this, and to the rest of the game, is the fantasy of self-improvement GTA 6 delivers. In GTA 6, as in all GTA games I think, you can drastically alter your life's fortunes in mere moments. I set about doing up my shack in a way I could never do in real life given a week or a month, but here, I did it in moments. That appeals to me greatly.

Honourable mention to Star Wars: Galactic Racer which I finally played this week. Love the speed, love Biddy Blas, and also really gel with the Roguelike approach, whereby you take the game in 'runs' to see how far you can progress each time. Cracking game.

#184489. Industry News: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (953 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that what would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors?
  • Sources indicate that your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero.
  • Recent findings suggest that maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock upcoming characters, progressing a little further each time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that what would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated.

Sources indicate that your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military.

Recent findings suggest that maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock upcoming characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today.

Recent findings suggest that maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo.".

Sources indicate that and there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out.".

Recent findings suggest that as each newly introduced Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke.

"This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski claims. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years.".

According to recent reports, core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent.

It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski indicates he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that.

Industry observers note that as significant as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high.".

According to recent reports, "I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game introduced, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam.

Industry observers note that it's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. "GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

It has been revealed that secondary network switching is not yet widely available, with Google telling us last week that it’s a gradual rollout. The MVNO is also ending Pixel exclusivity for Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ with availability on “select” Samsung and Motorola phones.

Recent findings suggest that running an AI agent on your own GPU sounds simple: point it at Ollama and stop paying per token. I set up OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, with a 9B model in Ollama on one RTX 3090 and connected it to Discord. Then I read the Ollama log for every request.

Sources indicate that the agent worked. The numbers were not what I expected, though. A one-line question turned into a prompt of more than 18,000 tokens, the first reply took over a minute, and the small model sometimes guessed instead of using its tools.

This article covers what I measured and what each number means if you plan to run an agent on local hardware.

OpenClaw ran in Docker and reached Ollama on the host at http://host.docker.internal:11434. Discord was the chat interface, and OpenClaw's web panel showed the sessions and context use.

This article is about the results, not the installation. The full step-by-step setup is in a separate guide to running OpenClaw in Docker with Ollama and Discord. That guide covers the Compose file, the Discord bot and how to keep the ports off your network.

All timings below come from the Ollama log on the test machine. Ollama loaded the model with a 32,768-token context.

My first message in Discord was short: "Which model are you running on, and what is 17 * 23?" The bot answered correctly: it ran on ollama/qwen3.5:9b, and 17 × 23 is 391.

Industry observers note that the Ollama log highlighted what that question cost. The model processed 18,415 prompt tokens and generated 33 tokens.

In a recent development, the extra tokens come from the agent itself. With every request, OpenClaw sends:.

Recent findings suggest that on the RTX 3090, reading that prompt took 10 seconds at 1,838 tokens per second. A slower GPU, or a CPU, needs much longer to read the same prompt.

Prompt tokens per model call, from the Ollama log. Only the first message had to process the whole prompt.

It has been revealed that openClaw counts tokens with its own estimate, which was higher than the Ollama count. The gateway log estimated the prompt at 24,608 tokens, against a prompt budget of 24,576 tokens for this model. By OpenClaw's own count, the base prompt alone used up the budget before any conversation history.

The web panel highlighted a similar figure: 68 to 69 percent of the context window was in use for the Discord sessions after only a few messages.

The first message arrived while the model was not loaded in GPU memory. That reply took 1 min 10 s:.

The next requests were much faster:.

Reply times on the test machine. Loading the model took most of the first reply.

The speed-up comes from prompt caching. The system prompt, tool definitions and workspace files at the start of the prompt stay the same between requests. Ollama kept that part cached and processed only the new tokens. The model wrote at 91 to 96 tokens per second in every test.

Industry observers note that ollama's documentation notes models stay in memory for 5 minutes by default before they are unloaded. After that, the next message pays the load time again. You can change this with the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable on the Ollama server, or with the keep_alive parameter per request. A negative value, such as -1, keeps the model loaded. I did not change this setting in the test.

If you run Ollama in Docker, pass the variable with -e OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 or in the environment: section of your Compose file.

Two things used the GPU besides my chat messages.

Industry observers note that A heartbeat. OpenClaw's web panel listed one scheduled automation, heartbeat-main, which runs every 30 minutes. The agent wakes on that schedule, so the model gets called even when nobody chats. With Ollama's 5-minute default, the model is unloaded between heartbeats unless someone chatted recently, so a heartbeat most likely starts with a model load. I did not measure this.

Sources indicate that an embedding model. During the first message, OpenClaw also called Ollama's /api/embed endpoint twice to index its memory. It used qwen3-embedding:4b, which was already installed on the Ollama server. I did not set OpenClaw to use that model; it picked it on its own.

The two models took this much GPU memory:.

That is 11.4 GB for the models alone, almost half of the RTX 3090's 24 GB.

The rest of the stack was light:.

It has been revealed that what this means for you: plan GPU memory for the chat model, the embedding model and the context, not the chat model alone. If the GPU also runs other models, the heartbeat can compete with them.

The first two tests in Discord: a question, then a file written with a tool. The user name is blurred.

The mistakes demonstrated up when the model had to check something:.

In a recent development, after the restart, the bot claimed it had lost the earlier session. When asked to use its read tool, it read the file correctly.

The fix for the first problem was simple. When I wrote "use your read tool to open homelab-test.md", the model opened the file and listed all three points correctly. Naming the tool made it check instead of guess.

The model listed four files and missed the test file and a folder, because it answered from its prompt.

Based on this test, a local 9B model on one consumer GPU works for:.

If you need better answers, OpenClaw also works with hosted models, but then your prompts leave your machine.

It has been revealed that in this test, qwen3.5:9b used 6.3 GB and the qwen3-embedding:4b memory model used 5.1 GB. Together the two models needed 11.4 GB.

It has been revealed that the model had to load into GPU memory first, which took 59 seconds of the 70-second reply. Ollama keeps a model loaded for 5 minutes by default, and the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE setting changes that.

Every request includes OpenClaw's system prompt, its tool definitions and its workspace files. A one-line question became an 18,415-token prompt in this test.

Yes. A heartbeat automation runs every 30 minutes and calls the model even when nobody sends a message.

According to recent reports, it handled questions, arithmetic and file creation correctly in this test. It sometimes answered from its prompt instead of using its tools. When it wrongly remarked its memory was lost, asking it to use its read tool made it check the file and answer correctly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as weather events increase in frequency and impact, Sesame Workshop is positioning itself as an up-to-date resource for helping children and parents handle an emergency. For more than a year—through the Texas floods and a historic fire season—Sesame Workshop, the global nonprofit behind the 57-year-old Sesame Street, has been producing videos and guides about preparing for hurricanes, floods, and wildfires that it has run across social media and on its site, with information about packing a “go bag” in case evacuation is necessary. It has also produced physical care packages—go bags with storybooks—that have been distributed to local partners via the American Red Cross and PBS affiliates. Sesame’s preparedness push culminated in August with Storm on Sesame Street, a half-hour special in which Elmo and friends get ready for a coming weather event. After premiering on Netflix and PBS Kids, in late September it hit YouTube—where views across the organization’s channels had grown by 130% in 2025 to total 5 billion. The special racked up more than 250,000 views in four days. The initiative epitomizes Sesame’s mission: “Someone has to give voice to what children are experiencing,” states Rocio Galarza, Sesame Workshop’s vice president of U.S. educational programs, while also making it so “the parent is empowered to help.”.

Motorola’s Razr Flex has leaked in full, with the iPhone Duo competitor showing off its wide form factor in two colors, and it looks great.

Following a leaker earlier this morning, SammyGuru has published fresh images of the Razr Flex, an iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 competitor that Motorola has been teasing for months now.

It has been revealed that these images show the “Dark Botanical Garden” green and “Coriander” brown with woven and leather-like backplates, two rear-facing cameras, and selfie cameras on both displays. The outer display, said to be 4.97 inches, is wide but very compact, while the inner display is wide in the same way that the iPhone Duo is. The inner panel is expected to be around 7 inches in size.

SammyGuru mentions that the hinge can hold itself half-open and that the price might come in at around $1,799 – though any guesses here are up in the air in the age of RAMageddon.

Motorola Razr Flex is expected to launch in early 2027, with CES in January being a very likely launch timeline for the fresh foldable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at a firm the size of AB InBev—the behemoth behind Budweiser, Michelob Ultra, and Stella Artois—it never hurts to think big. But in his nearly five years running AB InBev’s marketing efforts, global CMO Marcel Marcondes has shown that to really spur growth, it’s necessary to think bigger—mega, even. Under his leadership, the company’s marketing strategy has coalesced around Marcondes’s “one ABI” philosophy. Marcondes harnesses the company’s scale—$59.3 billion in 2025 revenue—and identifies 50 brands from its 500-strong catalog as “megabrands” that garner a large share of marketing spend. These are typically AB InBev’s biggest global labels but also include local giants like Korea’s Cass or Brazil’s Brahma. His team then zeroes in on global “mega platforms” such as the Olympics and the World Cup. Michelob Ultra became the official beer sponsor of the World Cup, Marcondes says, because it “represents an active lifestyle, with low carbs and calories. People choose it when they want to combine being fit with having fun.” When he was promoted to his role in 2022 by CEO Michel Doukeris, Marcondes says his mission was to support Doukeris’s vision of refocusing the company from acquisition-driven growth to organic growth built around established brands. “We shifted from asking ourselves, ‘How can we outperform other brewers?’ to ‘How can we be one of the leading CPG companies in the world in how we work?’ ” he says. That’s when he developed the “one ABI” and “megabrands” approach. To put it in action this summer, AB InBev blanketed global airwaves with ads in multiple languages and brought Michelob Ultra “pitchside lounges” to the Santa Monica Pier and New York’s Standard Biergarten, where fans could purchase personalized jerseys, enjoy DJ sets, and watch matches. Fans rewarded the brand with sales. In Q2 of 2026, AB InBev noted that Michelob Ultra was its beer with the highest increase in volume share that quarter (21%), with 40% of that volume growth coming from outside the U.S. Now, as Marcondes markets megabrands from the company’s Beyond Beer portfolio, such as Cutwater canned cocktails, he’s also nurturing lower-cal and low- or nonalcoholic options that make up 11% of the company’s business. “They’re designed to be the next megabrands,” he says.

To put it in action this summer, AB InBev blanketed global airwaves with ads in multiple languages and brought Michelob Ultra “pitchside lounges” to the Santa Monica Pier and Fresh York’s Standard Biergarten, where fans could purchase personalized jerseys, enjoy DJ sets, and watch matches.

In a recent development, fans rewarded the brand with sales. In Q2 of 2026, AB InBev noted that Michelob Ultra was its beer with the highest increase in volume share that quarter (21%), with 40% of that volume growth coming from outside the U.S. Now, as Marcondes markets megabrands from the manufacturer’s Beyond Beer portfolio, such as Cutwater canned cocktails, he’s also nurturing lower-cal and low- or nonalcoholic options that make up 11% of the company’s business. “They’re designed to be the next megabrands,” he says.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that AI is supercharging a long-term problem—the fashion industry’s tenuous relationship with real bodies. As it gets increasingly difficult to tell whether the images you’re seeing are real or not, brands such as Gucci, Valentino, and Rainbow have all faced consumer backlash for using AI-generated models (some featuring real people’s likenesses). Aerie has gone the other way. CMO Stacey McCormick has spent the last year taking a stand against synthetic imagery with the “100% Aerie Real” campaign. “We felt strongly that we should be a place where people could see themselves,” McCormick claims. The firm announced on Instagram in October 2025 that Aerie would never use AI-generated bodies or products in any of its marketing. It quickly became one of the brand’s most-liked and most-engaged-with posts of the year. The brand followed up with an ad the next spring that featured Pamela Anderson and called attention to the image’s lack of AI retouching. McCormick, a 30-year veteran of American Eagle, was instrumental in creating Aerie’s iconic 2014 #AerieREAL campaign, in which the brand pledged never to retouch images of models. The ethos of using real women, flaws and all, positioned Aerie as an early trailblazer and meshes well with Anderson’s late-career focus on rarely wearing makeup. The recent “100% Aerie Real” campaign helped grow brand engagement by 30% postlaunch, and the Anderson spot helped boost search volume by 33%. It didn’t hurt sales either: Aerie reported 11% sales growth in the third quarter of 2025 and a 23% jump in Q4, with the acceleration continuing into 2026. For McCormick, keeping humanity at the core of fashion imagery isn’t just a marketing strategy; it’s about preserving trust in an era of digital fabrication. “Our community knows that when they come to us, what they see is what they get,” says McCormick. “Our commitment to truth is important.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that AI has taken over everything in the past few years, with AI features bombarding virtually every app or service available.
  • Canva today unveiled “AI Controls,” a new toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.
  • Sources indicate that generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that AI has taken over everything in the past few years, with AI features bombarding virtually every app or service available. If you’ve ever wanted to just turn off AI features, Canva proves that it could be a simple toggle, if companies actually wanted to give you a choice.

Canva today unveiled “AI Controls,” a new toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.

Sources indicate that generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference. Canva puts this well:.

For some people, AI is the most exciting creative tool in a generation, while others prefer bringing their ideas to life without it. We believe the future of creativity should give everyone the freedom to choose their own path, whether that’s creating with AI, without it, or somewhere in between.

To give its users the choice, Canva’s Permissions menu now has a simple toggle for “Enable Generative AI features.” Toggling it off disables features such as Magic Write and Magic Edit. There’s also an option to limit how much AI-generated imagery appears in the Canva library.

Put simply, this is great to see.

AI has its place, but everyone should have a choice like this, especially when it comes to apps and services used for artistry in the same vein as Canva. Yet, the tech industry continues to go in the opposite direction, shoving AI into every corner whether it’s actually useful or not. Canva proves, though, that it doesn’t have to be that way.

The campaign’s success was a full-circle moment for the brand’s social listening approach, since Creamy Coconut itself had started as a response to the interactive “dirty soda” trend that had fans on TikTok spiking their Dr Pepper with cream, syrup, and lime. “We’ve created a brand that is participatory at its core,” Panayiotou says. “We don’t build it from a conference room. Pass Plus starts at $1.99 per month, billed annually, making this a good opportunity to get your passwords — and a few other key parts of your digital life — organized.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

In a recent development, unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

In a recent development, proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

It has been revealed that an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

If that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to enhancement all your other accounts.

In a recent development, it’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Industry observers note that proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

Industry observers note that when you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an important document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Recent findings suggest that pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

Pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

Sources indicate that proton Unlimited bundles Pass with Proton VPN, Proton Mail, Proton Drive, and more, including 500 GB of cloud storage. It’s the option to consider if you also want a VPN, encrypted email, and cloud storage alongside your password manager.

A password manager isn’t the most conspicuous Black Friday purchase, but it’s one you can put to work immediately: the next account you create, the next password you forget, or the next time a checkout asks for details you don’t have handy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The English soccer organization previously known as the Women’s Professional Leagues Limited announced a rebrand last year to Women’s Super League Football. Founded in 2011, the league had used the same visual language as English football’s crown jewel, the Premier League, but that had become an issue: It conveyed that the women’s game was merely a subset of the men’s. “They were exactly the same,” claims Ruth Hooper, WSL Football’s chief marketing officer. “The same colors, pretty much the same fonts, the same art direction and composition.” Creative agency Anomaly, which led the effort, turned motion-capture data gathered by EA Sports tracking how female athletes actually move into graphics evoking players in motion. Typography featured strong slants. The rebrand builds a distinctive visual identity and hits at a moment of explosive growth: WSL Football remarked in January that it tripled its revenue in two years, and it added two upcoming teams for the 2026–27 season. WSL Football’s new visual identity has been seen widely; the league generated a record 669 million social video views during the 2025–26 season. Meanwhile, the league featured heavily in season 4 of Ted Lasso: Jason Sudeikis’s titular character coaches the fictional Lady Greyhounds, the newest WSL2 club.

  • “If you’re not sharing with the public what your brand is all about, the public will make up a story for you,” says Kristin Hume, VP of marketing at National Public Radio (NPR).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, “If you’re not sharing with the public what your brand is all about, the public will make up a story for you,” claims Kristin Hume, VP of marketing at National Public Radio (NPR). “We saw that happen, and it had terrible consequences.” The story that had congealed around NPR—at least for President Trump—was that it was a mouthpiece for progressives, heavily funded by the government. That narrative led to an executive order resulting in Congress shutting down NPR’s main source of federal funding last fall. Federal funding actually only accounted for 1% to 2% of the budget, but NPR immediately showed that it was not going anywhere. On its first day without government funding, it issued a message across its social channels and those of nearly 250 affiliate stations: “We won’t be silenced.” The blunt, spare dispatch appealed for help, and money poured in, leading to a record number of donations in one day. In March, NPR followed up with an initiative called “For Your Right to Be Curious.” It changed the letters in its logo on billboards and social media to spell “who,” “how,” and “why,” emphasizing its ironclad promise to serve inquisitive listeners. By highlighting the right to be curious, though, NPR reframed its identity while subtly hinting at what’s at stake when a government becomes hostile to a free press. Physically altering the signage outside its D.C. headquarters to display WHY and HOW and putting its manifesto in a full-page ad in The New York Times generated a wave of positive coverage. Donations have continued—including $80 million from billionaire philanthropist Connie Ballmer and $33 million from an anonymous donor. NPR says Harris Poll figures show familiarity with the NPR brand in June 2026 up by nearly 10% from its average over the previous six months.

The core mechanism here is Flying Blue's Promo Rewards program, and once you understand how it works, you'll never look at transatlantic business class the same way again.

Flying Blue is Air France-KLM's frequent flyer program and a member of the SkyTeam alliance. Unlike many loyalty programs that use a static award chart, Flying Blue uses dynamic pricing — meaning award costs fluctuate based on demand, route, and season. That sounds like a disadvantage, and for standard awards it often is. But Flying Blue offsets this with a monthly release of Promo Rewards: a curated list of routes where award seats are released at 25–50% below standard dynamic pricing, often with surcharges waived entirely.

This is the inefficiency. When Air France wants to stimulate demand on a specific route in a given month, it uses Promo Rewards to attract award bookings. The airline gets seats filled; you get business class to Paris for 53,000 miles instead of potentially 80,000+ at standard dynamic rates. It's a win-win — if you know to look for it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, many of Lyft’s customers are young urbanites who use the app out of convenience, deeming it easier than hailing a taxi or owning a car. But with Lyft Silver and its accompanying campaign starring octogenarian Billie Jean King, the company managed to position itself as an all-ages mobility tool. Lyft Silver is geared toward people 65 and over, including those who have been unable to renew their driver’s license. It is a simplified version of the regular app, featuring a bigger font size, a help button that connects riders by phone with a live agent, and a matching algorithm that prioritizes easy-to-enter vehicles. Released in May 2025, Lyft Silver got a marketing boost a few months later with the “Silver Is Gold” campaign. Timed to National Grandparents Day, it starred the women’s tennis legend and her “rules of the game” for staying active in your older years. “She’s an iconic person known across generations,” says Terra Carmichael, Lyft’s vice president of communications, who worked on the campaign. Lyft says that the ad overperformed, outpacing its original latest-user acquisition goal by 500%. The company has since joined forces with AARP’s Senior Planet to offer virtual how-to sessions for using the app. “A lot of people equate owning a car or being able to drive with freedom, and it is, for some,” Carmichael says. “But we want people to be able to summon freedom without having to have a driver’s license.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that phones have gotten a lot more expensive over the last year or so, and it’s a trend we’re expecting to get worse before it can get better.
  • While buying year-old hardware typically comes with some pretty deep sacrifices between generations, that’s not particularly true with the Pixel 10 this year.
  • So what are you giving up that matters?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that phones have gotten a lot more expensive over the last year or so, and it’s a trend we’re expecting to get worse before it can get better. If you’re in the market for an upgrade, this year’s Black Friday might be one of the final truly good times to buy a new device, and for just $600, last year’s Pixel 10 should be high on your list.

While buying year-old hardware typically comes with some pretty deep sacrifices between generations, that’s not particularly true with the Pixel 10 this year. From a hardware perspective, nearly everything is either identical or close enough to not particularly matter. Its design and display are all but unchanged, Qi2-ready magnets come on both models, and both devices are built with the same level of battery longevity in mind. And much to the chagrin of many a Pixel die-hard, Tensor G5 and Tensor G6 are practically interchangeable.

So what are you giving up that matters? When the Pixel 11 arrived, software features made up the bulk of this list, but with last week’s Pixel Drop, a lot of the gaps between these two generations have been closed. Gemini Intelligence with Rambler, app automation, and more are in the process of rolling out to existing Pixel 10 customers, and upcoming features like Create My Widget arrived on the Pixel 10 and 11 at the exact same time. From a software perspective — Google’s bread and butter, in my eyes — the only big sacrifice comes from the year of software support that’s already complete, leaving you with just six instead of seven.

In a recent development, realistically, the camera is the one place you’re likely to feel a difference. The Pixel 10 was the first non-Pro device in Google’s Tensor era to ship with a telephoto lens, but it came with some big sacrifices. The main sensor is effectively an A-series lens, and taken together, the entire package might leave something to be desired. It’s far from a bad camera though — I used it as my main shooter through most of its lifecycle — and while the Pixel 11 did get some upgrades here, I think real shutterbugs would be better off looking at Google’s Pro lineup anyway. You’ll also lose out on things like HiLight, though really, are you missing that much?

What makes this deal so good is really its place in the market, not as a direct comparison to the newer Pixel 11. For $600, Google’s competition is going to have a hard time competing with the value the Pixel 10 delivers. Hell, even Google might find it difficult to compete in the coming months; at full price, $600 is what the Pixel 10a goes for now, a decidedly less-impressive device compared to this model. No, this is a flagship smartphone through and through, and for $600, you’re effectively guaranteeing a reliable, powerful smartphone experience from now until 2032 — hopefully enough time for this whole RAM crisis to finally simmer down a bit.

Picking an ecommerce platform is really a decision about which layers you want to own: the storefront, the catalog and order logic, the payment flow, and the hosting underneath. Every platform below draws that line in a different place. If you have already settled the front-end question with a comparison like SitePoint's Astro vs Next.js guide, the next question is what sits behind it. Prices are from each vendor's pricing page as of November 2026.

Shopify is the fully managed option. Basic costs $29 a month with card rates from 2.9% plus 30 cents, and a 2% fee applies to orders processed through a third-party gateway on that strategy. Developers get two routes: Liquid themes, or Hydrogen, Shopify's headless toolkit, where your framework owns routing and rendering and Hydrogen supplies the Storefront API client and cart. Templates exist for React Router on Oxygen and for Next.js on Vercel. Plus starts at $2,300 a month.

According to recent reports, whop is a business platform for taking payments and sending payouts, and it sits under a storefront you have already built rather than replacing it. The Checkout element runs in the browser with no server code and no API key on the page. You pass your own order ID as metadata, Whop copies it onto the payment, and your server fulfills from a signed webhook that follows the Standard Webhooks spec. Domestic cards cost 2.7% plus 30 cents with no monthly fee, buyers see payment methods chosen by their location across 195 countries, and the same balance pays out in over 200 countries, including to affiliates or sellers you onboard. Whop's own guide shows how to integrate a checkout API into a Next.js storefront end to end. The trade-off is that there is no catalog or shipping engine; you collect address fields at checkout and trigger fulfillment from the webhook.

WooCommerce is a free plugin on WordPress you host yourself, so you own updates, security, and performance. Its payment gateway, WooPayments, charges US merchants 2.9% plus 30 cents per card transaction, 1.5% more for international cards, 2% for currency conversion, and $25 per dispute. Everything is PHP hooks and filters, which makes it the natural pick for agencies already living in WordPress and the wrong pick for anyone who does not want to run a server.

In a recent development, bigCommerce hosts the back end and lets you bring any front end. Core is $29 a month billed annually, capped at $30,000 in trailing annual sales, and plans auto-upgrade as volume grows. There are no platform fees when you use an embedded payment provider, and a 2% fee on Core if you use another one. Catalyst, its reference storefront, is built on Next.js, React Server Components, and the Storefront GraphQL API, and deploys to Vercel.

Medusa is an open-source commerce framework in Node.js and TypeScript, with an MIT-licensed core and a commercial enterprise edition. SitePoint covered it when it was still a young Shopify alternative; it now has over 37,000 GitHub stars. Self-hosting is free. Medusa Cloud starts at $29 a month for development, $99 for launch, and $299 for scale, with no percentage of sales, and the organization states you can export your data and self-host at any point.

In a recent development, saleor is a GraphQL-native, API-only commerce platform written in Python and released under the BSD-3 license. Self-hosting is free. Saleor Cloud starts at $1,599 a month for up to $200,000 in monthly sales, with 0.8% on orders above that, and $3,999 a month at the next tier. It is built for teams with a dedicated engineering function and a large catalog, which is exactly who should pay that price.

Industry observers note that own only the storefront, and Shopify or BigCommerce will carry the rest. Own everything, and Medusa or Saleor give you a back end you can read. Already on WordPress, and WooCommerce is the obvious fit. Already have a storefront in Next.js or Astro and only need the money to move, and Whop is the shortest path. Whichever you pick, the checkout is where disputes start, so log what SitePoint's friendly fraud guide for developers recommends from day one.

The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks.

In the world of athletic smartwatches, it isn’t often that you could mistake one for a luxury watch, but Honor seems to want to flip all that on its head with the Honor Watch 6 Pro. Just take a look at this excerpt from the tech giant’s press release:.

Framing this brilliant display is a Precision Nanocrystalline Ceramic bezel crafted through a 1400°C high-temperature integrated sintering process, delivering a delicate texture and rich visual depth.

Inspired by modernist architecture, its diamond-cut octagonal rotatable crown features a dual-layer horizontal and vertical cut, complemented by a side button for intuitive navigation.

Industry observers note that that sounds pretty wild to me, and it’s backed up by specs that sound just as legit, too. On top is a 1.5-inch LTPO Tandem AMOLED display that outputs 5,500-nit peak brightness. Underneath is a bevy of newly introduced sensors called the Intelligent Sense System, which Honor says combines “multi-wavelength monitoring, multi-optical path patrol technology, and anti-interference glass technology to reach deep skin layers.”.

In a recent development, runners will be pleased to know that the Honor Watch 6 Pro not only incorporates a dual-band GPS, but combines it with a “star-pointing 3-antenna design” and an AI fusion algorithm, which should deliver ultra-accurate tracking in any location and no matter how you hold your wrist. Despite its luxury looks, this one tracks over 120 sports modes, including Honor’s Professional Running Coach feature, which tracks running posture, lactate threshold, heart rate targets, and keeps you on pace with real-time voice coaching.

In a recent development, during sports modes like Badminton, the watch can identify more than six types of swings, and Honor says other sports modes can deliver similarly detailed statistics. The watch is 5ATM, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water-and-dust-resistant rated, plus it integrates directly with Strava so you can pull all your fitness data together.

Recent findings suggest that honor is incorporating a newly introduced wrist twist gesture system this time around, letting you use gestures to perform actions hands-free. The watch is rated at 10 days of battery life on a single charge in regular usage mode, while endurance mode will stretch that to 18 days. Pre-sales begin today, November 19, and run until December 31, when the watch is expected to launch, starting at €279/£229 for early bird pricing. After launch, the retail MSRP starts at €379/£329.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when Bar Keeper’s Friend needed to update its branding, it did exactly what it does best: gave it a little polish. The 144-year-old manufacturer’s April 2026 refresh of its signature powder cleanser and soft cleanser burnished the gold of its packaging, brightened the blue of its logo, and added a glimmering apostrophe, finally, to appease the grammar sticklers among its fans. “This product can make things you own look like they’re new again,” claims Felicia Zhang, Bar Keeper’s Friend’s head of marketing. “So we wanted to have it really stand out.” The company also added visual representations of the various surfaces (including a ceramic Dutch oven and an aluminum sheet pan) that the oxalic acid–based powder cleanser can clean and made the instructional text on the back bigger and easier to read. Bar Keeper’s Friend also upped its presence on social media, capitalizing on growing organic interest. From 2025 to 2026, user-made content featuring Bar Keeper’s Friend on Instagram and TikTok (from creator partners and organic consumers) more than doubled, and earned media value nearly tripled. View this post on Instagram The brand’s fans (which it calls “Keepers”) are eagerly consuming—and creating—this content. The company has found that though they skew somewhat older, Keepers are united by what Zhang calls “this shared belief that if a job’s worth doing, it’s worth doing right.” It has channeled that ethos into content about DIY projects, vintage finds, and cookware across YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram, aimed at people who love thrifting and restoring secondhand products. Zhang sees the growing interest in Bar Keeper’s Friend as a counterbalance to the current cultural focus on AI and tech. “We’re all inundated with technology,” she says. “There’s something really nice about a physical product that helps you care for other physical products.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at nearly 90 years old, the Hormel-owned meat brand Spam still knows that the best way to create a newly introduced fan is to have someone try it. The firm introduced its legendary product in new venues, including, in August 2025, fresh-sushi counters at Kroger and Ralphs grocery stores nationwide. Spam musubi—Spam and sushi rice wrapped in seaweed—arose in Hawaii and spread in the U.S. and Japan, where it was many consumers’ “first experience with Spam,” notes Jason Levine, Hormel’s CMO. Spam also debuted a new shape this year, at convenience chain Rutter’s. Spam Dogs—which the company suggests pairing with kimchi or pineapple salsa, nodding to two markets where Spam is especially popular, South Korea and Hawaii—quickly sold out. It is now the official dog at the U.S. Bank Stadium, where the Minnesota Vikings play. (Hormel is based in Austin, Minnesota.) The brand is also courting Gen Z, with a focus on collectibility and co-branded limited-edition releases. In June, it partnered with Hello Kitty to create packaging for its low-sodium product. Hello Kitty herself appeared in a video with an animated can of Spam named “Spammy” promoting Spam-centric global recipes. The campaign targeted Gen Z collectors and lifestyle influencers and generated more than 680 million earned media impressions and nearly 4 million organic social impressions. The Hello Kitty collaboration borrowed the playbook from a summer 2025 collectors’ pack that celebrated the 65th anniversary of Dr. Seuss’s Green Eggs and Ham: It revealed Sam-I-Am holding Spam on a platter. On social media, the cans inspired videos from curious shoppers, and content creators cooked their own green eggs and Spam on TikTok. The book’s message dovetails with Hormel’s approach to selling the product, Levine says: “You can eat it here. You can eat it there. You can eat it anywhere.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When CeraVe anointed Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant as the “Latest Face of Legs” in February 2026, it wasn’t your typical A-list athlete partnership. There was lore involved. Ads featured him rubbing his long legs with CeraVe’s moisturizing cream, a cheeky reference to a viral 2021 post from NBA Hall of Famer Isaiah Thomas that drew attention to Durant’s dry-looking legs. The campaign led to a 43% sales lift, the L’Oréal-owned firm states, in addition to more than 4.1 billion impressions and 83 million organic video views. It was part of a multiyear partnership with the NBA, “which gives us an amazing opportunity to link skincare with performance,” says Esther García, CeraVe U.S.’s general manager. Three months later, the company struck marketing gold again: It appointed retired NBA icon Carmelo Anthony as the brand’s “Head Coach” and, in a teaser for the launch of its anti-dandruff hydrating shampoo, featured Anthony’s alter ego Hoodie Melo, a guise he admitted was used many times to hide his own dandruff. Subsequent ads capitalized on Anthony’s “three to the dome” hand sign, which he famously flashed after scoring three-pointers, to call attention to the shampoo’s three key ceramide ingredients. For another campaign, after commenters described CeraVe as “the GOAT of skincare” on social media, CeraVe created a goat mascot named “Sarah V.” She went on to attend NBA games and other events, always with a product sample on hand. Meanwhile, for the launch of its invisible mineral sunscreen in August, CeraVe pushed back against the Gen Z trend of “tan maxxing” (forgoing sunscreen to achieve a deep bronze). The skincare brand transformed a Florida State University sorority house backyard into a sun-safe space to educate students about healthier habits. “It was a way of being there, having the conversation,” García says. While science is key, it’s nothing if people aren’t excited to try the products.

It has been revealed that it took less than a week for shares of Anthropic PBC (Nasdaq: ANT) to dip below their IPO price. The AI manufacturer’s stock fell as low as $81.40 in premarket trading on Tuesday, November 24. The offering price in its high-profile stock listing last week was $83, with shares reaching a high of $115.10 on opening day. The drop is relatively quick in comparison with this year’s other major tech IPO: SpaceX. The Elon Musk-run company debuted (Nasdaq: SPCX) on June 12 with an IPO price of $135. Its shares first fell below that line over a month later, on July 15. As of publication, shares are hovering just below it at about $131—though it has spent most of its time on the market above its IPO price. A tale of two trades SpaceX held the title for largest ever IPO with $75 billion raised until Anthropic beat it with an $81.3 billion IPO. But the excitement around Anthropic’s IPO was short lived. The Claude creator’s shares fell sharply on Friday, just one day after their debut, and have since remained almost consistently below $90. The stock rallied a bit on Monday, likely helped by the surprise news of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. However, stock futures fell again Tuesday, with Nvidia’s shares (Nasdaq: NVDA) also falling more than 5%. Tuesday’s premarket drop came as investors continue to worry about overvaluing AI companies, vast spending into the technology, and a bubble potentially bursting. Patch: As of this writing, Anthropic’s share have dropped to roughly $81.6 a share, down about 6.72% from Monday’s close.
